description: LightGBM forecast of calciner outlet temperature (423CI400_TT_4), absolute value 60 seconds ahead
trained_by: nn_twin/plc_pipeline.py (sandbox outside this app) -- see backend/forecast.py for the feature engineering reproduced for live inference
target: 423CI400_TT_4 at t+60s (absolute degC, not a delta)

known_gaps_in_this_deployment.note: process_live's OPC mapping doesn't carry these 2 of 31 tags. backend/forecast.py imputes them from their process_1min long-run median and flags this in every response's imputed_tags field -- accuracy on live forecasts is degraded relative to test_metrics above until the live feed is remapped to include them.

live_deployment_backtest.how: python -m etl.backtest_forecast -- runs THIS repo's own backend.forecast.forecast_from_recent() (the exact function the live API calls) against real historical 1-second data from CSV_1S_PATH, scored against a Savitzky-Golay-denoised actual (matching how the training target was defined)
live_deployment_backtest.finding: training's 5.73 degC MAE was measured with CENTERED (non-causal) smoothing -- each historical point's denoised value used both past AND future neighbours. Live inference can only smooth CAUSALLY (no future samples for 'now'), which is a structural gap between the training evaluation and live serving, not a bug in this deployment.
live_deployment_backtest.bias_correction_attempted: tried applying the first window's -8.61 degC bias as a fixed additive correction to the second window: MAE got WORSE (2.81 -> 7.05), because the bias is regime-dependent, not a stable constant -- the same non-stationary-drift failure mode already documented for the LSTM soft sensor in nn_twin/. NOT baked into backend/forecast.py for this reason.
live_deployment_backtest.conclusion: honest expected live accuracy is closer to ~7 degC MAE than the training-reported 5.73, and will vary by period. Treat 5.73 as a best-case (centered-smoothing) number and ~7-9 as the live-serving range until the model is retrained with causal (one-sided) smoothing to match deployment reality.
